method: Evidence from the release files, compared with the reviewed 3.6.0; one Sonnet 5.5 agent established the facts with exact quotes; every quote checked against the release files and README by script; the facts that set the level checked again by hand; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads and runs uv's installer, and OpenAI's Codex CLI installer, when you press their install buttons
summary: When you press Install/Update Translation Environment, it downloads uv's install script from Astral and runs it (if you don't already have uv), then uses uv to build a Python 3.12 environment from a hash-locked package list, as its README says. For OpenAI sign-in, its install button (after a one-time notice) or update prompt likewise runs OpenAI's Codex CLI install script, which the README also says. Nothing checks either install script; on Windows they run straight from the web.

facts.what: The uv Python package manager's install script from Astral (astral.sh/uv/install.sh, saved to a temporary file and run with sh on Mac/Linux; install.ps1 piped into PowerShell on Windows), only if uv is not already found; then it builds a Python 3.12 environment and installs pdf2zh_next for full-document translation from a package list pinned by hash. Miniconda, which 3.6.0 downloaded first, is no longer downloaded.
urls: https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh (and its Windows script, for OpenAI sign-in)
facts.publisher: Astral, who make uv, and OpenAI, who make the Codex CLI
facts.readmeQuote: button installs a tested dependency set with `uv`
facts.notes: Trigger: the Install/Update Translation Environment button (id llm-tr-install-env, label trInstallEnv, line 34282) on the Translate tab: its click handler (60208) calls installOrUpdateTranslationEnvironment (58764), which calls installWithCatalog (58668), which calls ensureUvBinary (58186, called at 58673); ensureUvBinary runs installUv (58129) only when no uv is found. The only other caller of installOrUpdateTranslationEnvironment is TranslateController.setupEnv (58954). The Translate tab also checks for an update notice once a day, but that only reads a manifest and never installs. No confirm dialog was found for this button. Unchanged: the uv install script (UV_UNIX_INSTALL_SCRIPT, 58324: curl or wget of https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh to a temp file, then sh; Windows 58138: irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex) is run with no hash or signature check. Changed from 3.6.0: (1) Miniconda is gone: no download of repo.anaconda.com installers remains (3.6.0 downloaded Miniconda3-latest first and used uv only as a fallback; existing Miniconda environments are still found, 58029-58048, but nothing is downloaded for them). (2) The package install now uses uv to create the Python 3.12 environment, then 'uv pip sync <lock> --only-binary :all: --require-hashes' (58708), so each package file must match a hash in the lock. The lock and its manifest come from the developer's GitHub Pages (TRANSLATION_ENV_URL, 57803: https://visterainer.github.io/aidea-zotero/translate-env/manifest.json; the lock URL must be exactly requirements-<revision>.lock there, 57674-57676), the lock's SHA-256 is checked against the manifest (58491), and a bundled catalog with its own hash is the fallback (58339). The manifest and lock are fetched from the same place, so the hashes protect against a bad mirror, not against the developer. (3) Download-source choice: by preference or locale (Chinese locales) it can use the Aliyun PyPI mirror (57811) and the npmmirror python-build-standalone mirror (57812) for packages and the uv-managed Python (57764-57767); every file is hash-checked against the lock. The uv script itself has no mirror. README (lines 171, 173) says the button 'installs a tested dependency set with `uv`', so the download is told. Not covered by this finding: the provider-card 'Install/Update Env' button for the OAuth CLI (curl of chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh at 26621, behind its own OAuth notice, 54118), which 3.6.0 also had and which the scanner's evidence does not list.
facts.reviewerNote: Facts changed from 3.6.0: Miniconda removed, packages now hash-locked; the level-setting facts (official source, https, no check on the downloaded installer, click trigger, told in README) are the same, so the level and rule are unchanged.
facts.codexInstall: Also in 3.6.0 and not in that review: for OpenAI sign-in, tryInstallCodexStandalone (aidea.js 27352) runs OpenAI's Codex CLI install script from chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh (getCodexStandaloneInstallCommand, 26617), unchecked, in a hidden shell. It runs from the provider card's install button after a one-time notice (win.confirm(riskMessage), 54128 area; the notice says it downloads and installs OpenAI's official Codex CLI) or from an update prompt's Update button (runOAuthEnvUpdate, with a Later option). The README says so: 'Installs or updates the official standalone Codex CLI using OpenAI's install script.' Same facts as uv (the maker, https, you start it, told), so the level is the same.
